cluster_name: TikTok settles US DOJ children's privacy case for $400 million
tldr: Headlines across all nine source-countries converge on a $400 million legal settlement framed as a resolved legal obligation, with the financial magnitude providing the lead hook in most outlets. RT (Russia) is the sole divergence: its headline 'TikTok dodges US trial over children's data' reframes an agreed settlement as evasion of accountability — the only outlet treating the outcome as avoidance rather than penalty. BBC's 'one of largest child privacy settlements' is the only comparative that signals financial scale explicitly, while Taipei Times reduces the story to pure payment obligation. The Arabic-language France 24 uses a compulsion verb (تُلزم / obliges) where every English outlet uses agreement verbs (agrees, reaches, settles), assigning a more coercive framing to US authority.
event_summary: TikTok and ByteDance settled a US DOJ children's privacy lawsuit on 22 August 2026 for $400 million, one of the largest COPPA penalties on record; no admission of wrongdoing.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet whose headline frames the outcome as evasion ('dodges US trial') rather than payment or settlement — an adversarial framing that inverts the dominant narrative of legal accountability visible from titles alone.

bottom_line: Headline coverage treats the TikTok–DOJ settlement as a settled legal-financial fact, with the $400M figure as the near-universal lead hook; RT alone reframes the outcome as TikTok evading a trial, the one framing divergence detectable from titles alone.
